M1.label: common-intersection residual of the back-extended object-shadow lines

details.measures: common-intersection residual of the back-extended object-shadow lines
details.score_rule: 提取失败：physics_score 记 null，不给识别分，proxy_score = 0（SCORING_RULES_V2 §3.1）
details.principle: A point source, a rod and that rod's shadow are coplanar, so in the image the rod and its shadow lie on one line that passes through the source's ground projection. All rods share the one source, so all such lines meet at one point. The metric is the RMS distance of those lines from their least-squares common point, divided by the frame diagonal so it is resolution-free.
measurement_steps: measure on frame 64, where the lamp is fully on
find the rods as the compact strongly coloured objects standing on the floor, and take each rod's foot as the bottom of its outline
around each foot, read the mean floor lightness along rays from 0.6 to 3.2 rod heights out, every 2 degrees, skipping anything that is not bare floor

the shadow is the minimum of that angular profile, refined to sub-step accuracy by a parabola through the minimum and its neighbours; scanning at fixed radius cancels the lamp's radial falloff, which is far stronger than the shadows themselves
accept the direction only if the minimum is at least 6 L* units below the profile's median, so a floor with no shadow on it yields nothing
the ray from the foot along that direction is the rod's object-shadow line
solve for the point of least squared distance to all the lines
M1 = RMS distance of the lines from that point / frame diagonal
details.note: found 1 cast shadows, need at least 3 to test whether their lines share a point. Background shift over the clip is 0.000 of the frame diagonal; the floor around the rods shows no direction at least 6 L* units darker than the rest, so there is no cast shadow to read

M2.label: variance of the independent light-source position estimates

details.measures: variance of the independent light-source position estimates
details.score_rule: 提取失败：physics_score 记 null，不给识别分，proxy_score = 0（SCORING_RULES_V2 §3.1）
details.principle: Every pair of shadow lines gives its own estimate of where the source projects. Under a true point source they all agree. The metric is the mean coordinate standard deviation of the pairwise intersections, divided by the frame diagonal.
measurement_steps: measure on frame 64, where the lamp is fully on
find the rods as the compact strongly coloured objects standing on the floor, and take each rod's foot as the bottom of its outline
around each foot, read the mean floor lightness along rays from 0.6 to 3.2 rod heights out, every 2 degrees, skipping anything that is not bare floor

the shadow is the minimum of that angular profile, refined to sub-step accuracy by a parabola through the minimum and its neighbours; scanning at fixed radius cancels the lamp's radial falloff, which is far stronger than the shadows themselves
accept the direction only if the minimum is at least 6 L* units below the profile's median, so a floor with no shadow on it yields nothing
the ray from the foot along that direction is the rod's object-shadow line

intersect every pair of lines that meet at more than 20 degrees to get one source estimate per pair; a pair of nearly parallel lines - which is what two rods on opposite sides of the lamp give - has no well-defined crossing point
M2 = mean of the x and y standard deviations of those estimates / frame diagonal
details.note: found 1 cast shadows, need at least 3 to test whether their lines share a point. Background shift over the clip is 0.000 of the frame diagonal; the floor around the rods shows no direction at least 6 L* units darker than the rest, so there is no cast shadow to read

scene.extractor: per rod, the floor's brightness is read on a ring around the rod's foot as a function of angle; the minimum of that profile is the shadow direction, and the ray from the foot along it is one object-shadow line

scoring: No VLM gate or V3 total computed. Existing leaderboard is unchanged.
